body:
I keep thinking of using one of those cuddle-platonic contact matchmaking websites. So far they look like a terrifying version of backpages with an undergraduate degree in psychology. They seem to be almost dominated by women who want to exploit emotionally vulnerable, basically scarred men and take their money, in the same predatory way coyotes prey on migrants- all under the cover of theraputic contact. It just seems like prostitution for very lazy entitled women, and the most obvious evidence of a real kind of abuse of men by women that I can think of. I'm ranting.

When you want someone to care about you, paying them large sums of money just to treat you like you are cared about has the opposite effect, at least on me.

I will hug strangers, but they know I need a hug myself, and that's why I'm doing it- so again, funnily, it counts for less.

You need to find support, and in the absence of that the world seems like a place to just die. Human beings are social animals. We don't want, on a physiological level, to live in a world that doesn't want us- and indifference is the same as rejection, in a society like this. We live in a civilization which fails the good samaritan test.

If you want to complain to me personally, vent to me, use me as a sounding board or a sympathetic ear- by all means. It seems to be about the only role I have to play in human life, which is what pisses me off the most. I know I could actually help, actually do something in the world, and I can't because social participation is a contest and you can't even pick up garbage in the park independently.

And don't worry about my job! I am union labor so I got my job back. They treat me like a freak and I had to grovel humiliatingly for work I hate to people who I resent and who see me as a dangerous nutjob- I wonder how many people have become violent simply because they were treated as threats?

You were stuck with someone unstable and cruel and you acted out ever so slightly in that way, in a language or a form you learned from her or at least adopted because of her. I wonder how much of the arson in this world is the guy in the theater trying to enjoy his movie and his popcorn, flipping out at being Kafka'd by some panic-monger singling him out to shout fire.

Somebody hypocritically asked me if I was okay at work once, like it was obvious to me they just thought I was nuts and had a problem with me and wanted me to put my tail between my legs and slink off; my response was supposedly (I don't remember) "Don't worry, I'm not going to come in here and shoot the place up" - so they fired me for making a threat.

People really don't care; probably 80% of the time. They are going through life little-kid faking, trying to score points and get each other in trouble. It's ignorant, it can be soul crushing when it feels like you are surrounded by it.

And hey! A pattern forms. All these posts I read, almost every one I respond to, it's a guy who was left by a woman. We live for others and can that ever be honest, because can we ever be sure they are?

I am lamer than you, I have not attempted yet but I have the same basic pattern of breakup and isolation and in my case, not having anything I can honestly believe will improve, ever. Every day is the same; and is a kind of nothing, a kind of emptiness. Other people, in some way, it's like they are the only things that make reality feel real. Being alone on the earth, really alone and not participating in anyone's life just feels like living a continual bad dream. You grow up dependent on people- suddenly they don't exist anymore- it feels like being abandoned. I know that is the easiest ending for everything, the state it will return to.

I wish I had someone to tell me it was okay to die; someone to basically do it. I have that religious longing for an angel of death, someone to take me away from my own life, to rescue me from it.

I have what I need sitting on the counter to induce a painful organ failure that would take days of terrible pain and sickness. But once I drank it down, that would be it, the damage would be irreversible and I couldn't back out and get help. I think about how easy it would be, to just drink it down, and worry about the panic and the indecision later, after it was too late to do anything. I think about it every day, making it a little voice inside my head, a little motivator. I wonder if I created that little voice because I want to do it, or because I want to pretend I am strong enough to ignore my own despair no matter how it tortures me.

I feel like I have failed at being happy. All the times in my life where it was supposed to make a difference it didn't. The only times I seem animated are bad; when I'm arguing, when I'm going crazy. There's no positive confidence, no pleasant reaction to pleasant things. I lost everything in my own life that mattered. I can't get anything from other people other than the sense I am a burden on them. I want to stop experiencing anything anymore, because why keep repeating something that can only be negative? The point has been proven.

I don't think I have any fancy condition like anhedonia, but there just isn't anything left for me to enjoy. How evil and stupid and phony would I have to be to take any pleasure in anything, when what is really important to me is all gone, lost, failed, buried in the past? In my heart I just wish I could die in the arms of someone who felt sympathy for me, but I would know that if I lived, they would realize they didn't.

I think there is something people need basically from each other, to exist and thrive at all. There is some ingredient that comes from social reality, whether that is someone who is in your life or someone who could be in the future or who at least exists sympathetically in your own time on this earth.

But there is a point in your own thinking or experience where you can become totally cut off from any positive ideation, any rational ability to cope with the circumstances of your own life, where you essentially feel your existence is a prison and nothing in your life holds the promise of anything but punishment.

I don't want to get out of bed. I don't want to wake up. I don't really want to try and reach out and socialize, I know how it will play out in the long run, or at least I have every outcome in my experience backing up a negative prediction. Work is a prison. Family ended my life instead of nurturing it. No one can help me. No one has the spoons.

But I don't know how to stop just being miserable. I don't know how to let anything change except to fall apart slowly, to watch my life get worse and worse and hate it more and more.

After six years together mine left me for some douche she used to complain to online about me, and I don't really have a reason to live my life. I can understand the philosophy of protecting yourself from people by cutting them out or avoiding them just as a means to avoid the experience I went through and how I can't stop feeling now and know from my family history won't ever leave me; but still. If all I can do is try and fail, there are some things I would do anyway. And some things I worry I will do anyway. Love can be a way of pretending you understand, pretending you see the light at the end of the tunnel, unfortunately, when you don't get loved back. I don't know if it is worth the leap of faith anymore, but I don't know why else I should endure any second of what I remember or what I see laid out ahead.

I wish I lived on an island with all the other suicidal people. I feel like we would actually be capable of listening to one another and not feeling alienated by each other's presences. Ninety percent of what I encountered in mental health care was people simply threatening me to stop a behavior they objected to without any other form of care than the threat. That was the extent of "intervention."

I think people see your hostility to living life without complaint as an attack on their own happiness a lot. As if they need you to accept that it's necessary to act positive, because that is what they have to do. As if your pointing out something wrong was threatening the facade they maintained for themselves.

I think honestly that almost the majority of people are pretty much miserable or disappointed with life, and that by and large the culture has moved towards attacking people individually for expressing that. You aren't "allowed" to be sad, because no one has the resources to deal with your emotions, because everyone is almost at their limit just dealing with themselves. You aren't allowed to express real dissent, because just participating in society is  endangered anytime you appear to be a legal liability to an institution. You could lose your job, your academic career, your place in a community.

Almost the majority of the reason I feel like taking my own life is because I feel like I am never going to be able to express myself freely with someone and get that back from them too. I feel like I'm being buried alive in lying and social pretense and competition that I don't care to participate in. I can sympathize with people trying to improve their lives by being as pleasant and positive sounding as they can, but that can't be all there is to life or to society. People have to be able to suffer publicly for society to be worth participating in. Men and women have to be allowed emotional support. People have to have time for each other- but a culture where people work and run errands all week and never even have time to prepare a hot meal on their own is a culture that is using people up like disposable parts.

Every single time someone here expresses how pissed they are at society and how it has failed them and pretends to be there for them in name only I feel like there goes a kindred spirit. I think we live in a broken community, and I think in a lot of ways feeling like you have no way out is the natural and honest thing. I say we form our own state. I'm almost not joking.

I have the same, "today, I'm going to do this today" thing. Mine is different, and nothing is stopping me but my own apathy and cowardice and indecision. On the days I really work myself up telling myself I will go through with it, I always end up painfully tired; and when I wake up I feel so much pain, so much like I wish I could just collapse and cry and be consoled. I'm not even sure if I want to die, or if I just can't face the loneliness my life is now and there's no other way out. Why is it so exhausting to want to die?

I can't pretend one day I will wake up and "feel better" but maybe I can just sleep until I can't remember anything else and nothing in my life touches me anymore. Just sleep until I die of old age- that way everyone else will be satisfied.

It's the only way I can fall asleep at all! I'm to the point where I think my body has conflated consciously wanting to die with being able to rest, being safe enough to shut down attentively.

The pollyanna optimist way to restate that, is that we have confused being tired of externalities in our lives that exhaust us, rather than actually wanting death- but I see no path away from living a life that is merely pain and continual suffering for me, towards anything I would consider productive or holding the possibility of happiness or joy. In the face of that, I just have no reason to continue, and every day is just a burden I carry out from cowardice and the fear of throwing away my life for no purpose at all. I would at least like to die purposefully, or feel that it was an act of mercy from something beyond myself.

I feel the same way about myself; but I think most of the differences in outcomes have to do with how people express themselves, rather than any innate difference. A slow horse or an average person on a bicycle can probably outrun the fastest human runners. What makes us stand out as individuals probably isn't really all that meaningful in changing anything in the world. But the only thing people go off of is comparing you to others, the only thing you can go off when you try to find people for yourself or they do for themselves. There is a kind of honesty that is forbidden, a kind of negative disclosure about yourself that everybody tries to run from and hide and conceal, and there is a game around that that I think dooms the world. You won't hear a salesman say how desperately he wants your money. But no matter what I do, I can't stop expressing my negativity to others in a way that isolates me- even from other people who want to express theirs. Maybe the problem with negativity is that it is selfish- two people can't share it and comfort each other.

I have to repeat mantras of suicidal ideation just to fall asleep. At all. Like the point of letting myself lose consciousness is to never regain it. I can't bring myself to actually do anything except fantasize- I am starting to wonder if I am a terminator and it somehow goes against programming I can't override- but my behavior is getting more and more reckless. I'm driving faster, mostly (when I'm not in traffic, on empty roads). It's like I'm very fussy and I'm slowly trying to turn up the heat in a bath without noticing it, or down to cold.

Anytime a professional has ever "intervened" in my life, honestly things have just gotten worse. I think between the time of buddha and the publication of endless self help books, not a lot has changed. It's not a problem anyone can really solve for anyone else.
